author: Edward Segal
title: Minot man in custody for manslaughter after death of 6-year-old - NewsBreak
text:
By Edward Segal No media credit provided. ,
6 hours ago
MINOT, ND ( KXNET ) — A Minot man has been arrested and charged with manslaughter after the death of a six-year-old, allegedly stemming from injuries he inflicted on her as a baby.
According to arrest documents obtained by KX News, Matthew Zappone was arrested this week and is facing five felony charges after previously serving time on an assault charge related to the child, identified as his daughter.
The girl was first admitted to Trinity Hospital in Minot in 2016 for a suspected seizure when she was two months old. Arrest documents show the hospital found several medical issues, including a concern with her rib x-rays and mild to moderate dehydration.
A day later, she was admitted to the Pediatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU) at Sanford Hospital in Fargo, and diagnosed with conditions including a subdural hematoma — or bleeding near the brain — a seizure, and retinal hemorrhage of both eyes. She was also found to have a fractured skull and multiple broken ribs.
Unreleased interview, intoxication evidence at center of Minot murder case According to the Cleveland Clinic , a subdural hematoma is usually caused by a head injury.
A social worker was then called to take a look at the two-month-old and complete a report of child neglect and abuse.
Zappone was charged with Class C felonies for child abuse and neglect, and pleaded guilty to assault in 2018. He was sentenced to five years in prison, of which three were suspended.
The arrest report says that in May 2023, after years of seizures and multiple other health issues, the girl died at the age of six. An autopsy report showed the cause of death was homicide based on the injuries she sustained as a baby.
Zappone was arrested this week and now faces Class B felonies for manslaughter and aggravated assault, as well as Class C felonies for negligent homicide, assault, and reckless endangerment.
His initial court appearance is scheduled for February 3.
